item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits Made. See Discussion Below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

The WikiWalk team recieved the following crosslink proposal from psul:

This is a Heritage article, and already contains several crosslinks (to SCP-271 and SCP-217). However these exist in a tight loop of Series I articles that link within themselves (and to SCP-229) but not elsewhere on the site. Adding a link to a Series III article, which itself links to a range of pages containing many further links (the AIAD hub with tales and SCPs, the Little Mister series), will connect the Heritage part of the site to a wide range of articles from all site eras, serving the precise purpose of the project.

Within the article itself, the additional text helps resolve an ambiguity / illogicality in the original Description. Originally, the Foundation pulls 882 out of the salt water, it resumes motion, and "after several accidents" it is cut down. The Foundation comes across as a little inept - it doesn't re-submerge 882 and cut it underwater, instead letting it grind up personnel whilst running freely in the open air. By using SCP-2519 to reduce 882's motion, the Foundation don't have to cut it underwater (which would be much more expensive) and reduce the risk of accidents. This solution also reinforces Dr Gears' characterisation as a precise but lateral-thinking problem-solver.

The suggested text and changes are below:

After several accidents, SCP-882 was cut down and contained on site.

Which I'd suggest amending to read:

After several accidents, Dr. Gears authorized SCP-2519 to be played on loop, which successfully reduced the object's motion, enabling safe access. SCP-882 was then cut down and contained on site.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Perhaps I've addressed this poorly in the main entry, but what i was trying to get across with the "driven crazy" aspect is that it's like a infection. You don't have to bathe 24/7 in the virus to catch it…you just have to be exposed once. The clanking and grinding will develop in you over time, once it's "taken root", so to speak. You can hopefully avoid it with short, limited exposure…but much like avoiding a cold when the whole office is sick, it's just a matter of time and luck. Turn up unlucky, and you'll have the sound of a full bore auto plant, all mashed in to a small room, in your head, and the only way to lessen it is to feed the thing.

I always imagined that it's recoverable, over time…but it's very, very hard. I imagine restraints and lots of observation would be needed for someone "drying out" from exposure. Even then, I'd imagine that a person so exposed would carry some kind of "scar" for the rest of their lives.

Also, who's to say it's not growing in to…something? Maybe it's like a starfish, a small shard of a greater whole, trying to regrow. Or perhaps not…the reason the article doesn't go in to much detail, is to allow people to make up the details. I've found that, given the chance, a person's brain will often cook up much, much worse and personal horrors then I could ever try and explain.

Still, if it doesn't work for you, it doesn't work, and all the more power to you. You can please everyone some of the time, or some people all of the time…i shoot for the middle ground. Hopefully something else i write can give you the jibblies…and if not, that's OK too. Thanks for taking the time to let me know your feelings, at least…

First off, as someone that works with machines, the very concept of a collection of gears and mechanisms with no visible purpose or power source that runs on its own, and not only instantly adheres to metal objects but actually integrates them into itself - instead of just, y'know, jamming up and breaking - is terrifying in its implications.

Then you add the fact that it not only does all this, but that it can (to a point) repair damage to itself like a body heals, and the only way it can be contained is keeping it rusted in sea water (SPECIFICALLY sea water, to boot) and that it psychically compels people to worship it… Yeah, that's the scare factor there.

You may as well say "I don't see what's so special about pizza, it's just dough with some cheese and sauce."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well…

I saw 173 on /x/, ages ago. Read it, opened the picture, CLOSED THE PICTURE, then went and did something else. Quickly.

Image stuck in my head for a while, and eventually, once i saw one or two other items being posted, said "damn it, i think i can do this…"

Ended up posting…11-12 items over a period of about a week. The first was 882. After doing so, I figured I needed some kind of tripcode, just so people knew it was me.

went with "COG".

When we made the migration from board to wiki, i kept the same name for a while, but with everyone taking "docter" this, and "Agent" so and so, i didn't want to be the one going against the grain. I just went for something quick, easy, and somewhat like my old name…

Therefor, Doctor Gears.

Also, i owe the good doctor's emotionlessness to /x/ as well. Posted a "letter" involving Dr. Gears on /x/, long, LONG before "support documents" really existed…and got shot down for sounding too dramatic and such. I figured "Well, i'll put an end to that…", and…well, there you go.

…sorry for the random history lesson…
